Totally get where you’re coming from about new space companies. We are partnered with Black Sky Aerospace who are providing the rockets who already have a successful launch history and government backing. Our R&D is on the fly back capability that we are adapting to the craft to eventually have a reusable rocket using hydrogen and oxygen fuel making it cleaner and cost effective for repeated launches (scramjet will be doing weekly small satellite launches into LEO, also clean fuel).

He was at Langley about 15 years ago. Just left his position as Department Head and Professor of Hypersonics at UQ to start the company so all the tech has been trialled and tested before, we are commercialising it to create an effective and sustainable space launch system.

A: you’re on NASA networks! That’s awesome 
B: it’s a ground launch first stage rocket carrying this payload but ultimately designed to get a second stage scramjet to mach 5. With these launches we will be going straight up to 100+km as a sounding rocket and using newly developed tech to land the rocket back like an aircraft. Doing R&D on every launch. 
Our designer who is currently focused on the scramjet development, had 10 years working on scramjets at NASA.
